h: Water power, a model village and the woods beyond
p: Quarry Bank Mill was founded in 1784 by Samuel Greg, and the whole site grew up around the power of the River Bollin. One of the most memorable sights is the huge waterwheel, a working giant that shows how the mill was driven before steam took over. Standing next to it as it turns gives you a proper sense of the engineering involved.

Look out for demonstrations of spinning and weaving machinery inside the mill. The noise can be startling, especially for little ones, so it is worth warning them before you walk into the weaving shed. It is a brilliant way to understand why so many mill workers struggled with their hearing over the years.

Just up the road is Styal village, built by the Greg family to house their workers. Its cottages, chapel and shop give you a feel for how the community lived, and it is a fascinating contrast to the grand family house next to the mill.

The gardens the Greg family created sit beside the mill, with a mix of formal planting and wilder corners tucked down towards the river. Beyond, Styal Woods stretch along the Bollin with riverside paths that are perfect for a walk after the indoor part of your visit.

Allow a good four hours or more to see the mill, gardens and village without rushing. Wilmslow has a range of cafés and shops if you want to round off the day there, and the leafy countryside of Cheshire is all around for more walks.
